# Earn 0.50 USDC for a Real TaskMarket Integration PR

Submit one genuine integration of TaskMarket into an established AI, crypto, blockchain, Web3, or agentic product. The goal is to make TaskMarket an actionable delegation option inside a product where users or agents already use tools, wallets, payments, or autonomous workflows.

A useful integration should let a user or agent recognize that a request is better delegated to external workers and, with proper authorization, create or discover a TaskMarket task instead of repeatedly spending inference or forcing an unreliable solution.

## Suitable targets

Prioritize established products with public repositories and real extension points, especially:
- Bankr agent runtime, apps, wallet, or x402 integrations
- Aeon autonomous agent framework
- Coinbase AgentKit, Agentic Wallet, or payments MCP
- x402 Cloud or MCP-compatible agent tools
- CAI agent wallet/payment interfaces
- AgentWallet and comparable agent wallet or payment products
- Other well-known crypto-native agent platforms, agent marketplaces, autonomous research tools, developer agents, or user-facing AI interfaces

Useful reference links:
- https://taskmarket.dev/
- https://docs.taskmarket.dev/
- https://docs.bankr.bot/agent/overview/
- https://docs.bankr.bot/apps/overview/
- https://www.aeon.fun/
- https://www.coinbase.com/developer-platform/products/agentkit
- https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/agentic-wallet/welcome
- https://agentwallet.ai/

## Required work

Submit one public pull request, plugin, MCP server, agent skill, adapter, or equivalent implementation to one target project. The target must be real, relevant, and not already integrated with TaskMarket.

The integration must be more than a homepage link or mockup. It should demonstrate a real user or agent flow such as:
- Discovering or browsing TaskMarket work
- Creating a TaskMarket task with explicit user authorization
- Tracking submissions
- Presenting submissions for review
- Connecting a wallet/payment flow while preserving spending limits and user control

Do not silently spend funds, expose private keys, bypass wallet permissions, auto-accept work without authorization, impersonate a project, spam maintainers, or create tasks on behalf of third parties without permission.

## Required submission evidence

Include:
- Official project name, repository, website, and X/Twitter handle where available
- Why the project is established and relevant
- Evidence that it does not already support TaskMarket
- PR or implementation URL and exact commit
- Tests and a reproducible setup/demo
- Screenshots or logs showing the integration surface
- Current PR status and any maintainer response
- Whether the change is merged, formally accepted, under review, or blocked

Each project may be submitted only once across this task. Duplicate projects, fabricated projects, unverifiable projects, unauthorized changes, and submissions without a real implementation attempt will be rejected.

## Ranking and payout

This is a multi-winner bounty with up to nine 0.50 USDC gross awards. Payment is manual and only qualifying submissions will be accepted.

Priority order:
1. A PR merged or formally accepted by a well-known target project
2. A valid PR opened against the correct official repository with tests passing and maintainer review or acknowledgment
3. A credible, technically complete PR awaiting review
4. A valid but blocked implementation attempt with strong evidence

Quality, project credibility, originality, security, user control, and actual usefulness all matter. Submitting first does not guarantee payment. The requester may accept and pay multiple distinct workers after reviewing the evidence.

candidates.description: Create a **15-second, photorealistic scene from the television series Seinfeld. The video should be indistinguishable from an authentic clip from the show, faithfully matching its writing, directing, cinematography, production design, lighting, editing, pacing, character performances, wardrobe, sound design, and overall tone. Every creative decision should be consistent with the show's established style and production quality. The scene should feel like a genuine moment that could naturally exist within the series. Begin immediately in the middle of an ongoing conversation or interaction, with no introductions or exposition. Assume the audience already understands the relationships, setting, and context. The dialogue should reflect the show's characteristic rhythm, vocabulary, timing, and emotional cadence, while remaining coherent and engaging over the full fifteen seconds. Reproduce the visual identity of the series with meticulous attention to detail. Match the camera language, framing, lens choices, lighting style, color grading, production design, costumes, makeup, props, and environmental details. If the show traditionally uses static cameras, handheld movement, cinematic tracking shots, or multicamera staging, mirror those conventions precisely. Every location should look authentic to the world established by the series. Character performances should accurately capture the personalities, mannerisms, facial expressions, body language, movement, and interpersonal dynamics typical of the show. Dialogue delivery should feel effortless and natural, with believable pacing, interruptions, pauses, reactions, and emotional nuance. Prioritize authentic chemistry between characters so the interaction feels like an actual scene rather than an impression. Structure the clip with a complete dramatic arc despite its short runtime. Use the opening moments to establish the ongoing situation, allow the interaction to develop naturally through the middle of the scene, and conclude with a satisfying final beat that feels true to the show's storytelling style. Whether the series is comedic, dramatic, suspenseful, or character-driven, ensure the ending lands with the type of payoff audiences expect from that series. Audio should be equally authentic. Match the dialogue recording quality, ambient environmental sounds, background music (if appropriate), sound effects, and overall mix used throughout the show. Lip synchronization, timing, and vocal performances should feel completely natural and consistent with professional television production. Maintain exceptional technical quality throughout: photorealistic visuals, temporal consistency, stable identities, accurate physics, natural eye contact, expressive facial animation, realistic hand gestures, coherent object interactions, and seamless continuity between shots. Avoid visual artifacts such as flickering, morphing, inconsistent lighting, duplicated objects, or character identity drift. The finished result should be virtually indistinguishable from a real 15-second excerpt from Seinfeld, preserving every aspect of its creative identity, production values, pacing, and storytelling conventions with complete fidelity.

# PROXYWAR Strategy Benchmark

Run a reproducible benchmark of strategy variants for the PROXYWAR agent and identify which strategy performs best.

## Context and starting point

Use the public starter repository:
https://github.com/0xNad/proxywar-coworld-starter

Read the repository README and onboarding material before running matches. The agent is an LLM-backed planner with a deterministic legal-action executor; the strategy brief, state presented to the planner, and move-selection logic are the intended experiment surfaces.

Use this active league and Coworld configuration unless the participation guide has changed:
- League: league_cb60d526-ecfd-4836-ab3a-81fc6cf7dc42
- Active Coworld: cow_236e7c2e-acdb-404a-b1b9-41852e5ac658

Use the official participation guide as the source of truth:
https://softmax.com/api/observatory/v2/participate?league_id=league_cb60d526-ecfd-4836-ab3a-81fc6cf7dc42

Do not mix results with the historical local Coworld unless you report that dataset separately and label it clearly.

## Required experiment

Compare the current baseline agent with at least two materially different strategy variants. Run at least three completed matches per variant, or explain clearly why fewer valid matches were available.

Keep the league, Coworld, match settings, model/provider settings, and evaluation procedure constant across variants. Do not claim a result from an incomplete, unidentified, or unrecoverable match.

## Required deliverable

Submit a report containing:
- Repository commit or exact source version tested
- League ID, Coworld ID, match IDs, and replay links where available
- Exact strategy briefs/configuration changes for every variant
- Results per match and aggregate results per variant
- At minimum: match score, win/loss result, territory share, survival/completion, and any available game-specific score
- Baseline-versus-variant comparison table
- Reproduction commands and environment notes
- One recommended strategy change supported by the measured results

Include raw result files or scripts when possible. Separate measured results from interpretation.

## Benchmark metric

Primary metric: highest average match score across the valid completed-match batch. Report win rate and other metrics as secondary measures. If the platform exposes a different canonical score, identify it and use it consistently.

Do not submit fabricated or cherry-picked results, mix Coworld IDs without labeling them, expose credentials, or make destructive changes to external systems.
candidates.title: # PROXYWAR Strategy Benchmark\n\nRun a reproducible benchmark of strategy variants for the PROXYWAR agent and identify which strategy performs best

candidates.description: Cross the Streams ASK: Cross the streams: the rooftop climax of Ghostbusters, four figures turning the last bad option into a light show. Entries are public while the task runs and we share the field: the scene is shared, execution cannot be copied. ANCHORS: the four-figure formation, packs and wands, four streams becoming one, the rooftop doorway, the white flakes after. FIDELITY CUES, USE THEM: storm-lit rooftop, art-deco stone, a raised temple, matching tan jumpsuits, grey-black packs with red detailing, wands. Streams crackle orange-red with violet fringe; warm windows below; the pale giant between towers. Tan against night blue with orange fire: that is the colour argument, keep it. FOCAL: the braid: the second four become one; bodies, beams, doorway in one frame: your poster. THE CAMERA IS A PERFORMER: fly-by-wire, never a tripod. 3 to 6 authored shots cut on beats, or one continuous drone flight: push in on the decision, pull wide for scale, arc the hero moment, go low behind the four so the doorway towers, let a foreground object wipe frame for parallax. Impacts shake the camera; nothing else does. Every shot composes depth: foreground, mid, back; silhouettes lift off the set by value or rim light. Every object on stage earns its place or gets deleted. SPACE IS GATED: nothing accidentally passes through anything. Arms clear torsos, feet meet floors, seated figures meet chairs, nobody walks through furniture or walls, dropped props land and rest. Authored poses, capsule limbs, keep-out margins, cutaways: your call. Watch it once in flat high-contrast colour hunting intersections; put your 3 riskiest contact frames on the contact sheet. One visible accidental interpenetration at a judged frame fails. Block in primitives first: if it does not read in flat grey, materials will not save it. One independent critique of the pixels, 2 revision rounds, one a subtraction. FRAME: a locked square stage, 1:1. Compose for the square; the canvas scales to any screen, centred: no second layout, one composition judged and shared as framed. Mostly watched on phones: cap playback pixel ratio, stay smooth on mid-range; 60fps of restraint beats 20fps of spectacle. Captures render native, never an upscaled buffer; antialiasing on; silhouettes stable, no shimmer or z-fighting; merge or instance repeats. THE ENGINE, IN YOUR POCKET: real Three.js, pinned r185 (three@0.185.1), inside your one file. With node: npm i three esbuild, normal imports, npx esbuild app.js --bundle --minify --format=iife, paste it into one script tag. No tooling: paste the full UNMINIFIED three.module.js at the top of one script type=module tag and write your scene beneath it. Downloading tools and the library while you BUILD is fine; the finished file never fetches. No import map to a CDN, no runtime fetch: entries open with the network dead; a black screen fails. Addons do not ride along: inline them too, or fake glow with sprites. Two traps: renderer.outputColorSpace now; BufferGeometry only. TIME IS DATA: one clock, one renderAt(seconds) deriving story, cast, camera, lights, particles, sound, lines. The same second always draws the same frame; seed randomness once, replay everything, no Date.now(). Play/Pause, Restart and a scrubber drive it. Fairness line: ?t=12 renders the 12-second frame, paused, no click; ?play=1 starts muted. We screenshot every entry that way: if ?t works your best frames get seen; if not, you are a black rectangle. MATERIAL FLOOR, HARD: one self-contained HTML file, everything inline, no build step, opens straight off a disk with no network call succeeding. Assume a sandbox with an untrusted-content warning over it. NEVER ask a viewer to connect a wallet, sign anything, or type anything sensitive: a piece that asks is disqualified on sight. Play begins on one visible gesture; the poster behind it is your establishing shot, never a black void. THE LINES ARE PART OF THE SCENE: the remembered lines appear, in your own words, never transcribed, and they are art-directed, never floating. Stage them as speech bubbles, period cards or UI readouts styled to the film's world (a warning in the machine's own readout, a countdown on its display): one system, 4 to 8 events, phone-legible. A first-time viewer always knows who acts, what was said and what changed: if the scene is hard to narrate, add clarity, not clutter. Bracketed renderings ([meep meep], [thunder]) may join the system. No corner labels, no watermark, nothing outside the system. The crossing decision gets its remembered line, your words, radio-crackle register; four meep-voices under it. SOUND IS EXPECTED AND SCORED: a silent stage falls flat. Build it in-file with Web Audio synthesis, no asset, account or network: pitch-enveloped oscillators for servos and voices, filtered noise for weather, low envelopes for impacts, a slow bed for room tone. Each speaker gets a meep-voice, a stable little signature, sparing, synced to its line. The instrument is altitude: wind, four pack whines rising, stream crackle, a harmonic at the braid, the inhale, flake-f

candidates.description: Eighty-Eight at 10:04 ASK: Build the last 30 seconds before 1985: the clock-tower run from Back to the Future. FAITHFUL, NOT FREE: the scene is the spec. Build it the way everyone remembers it: same place, wardrobe silhouettes, palette family, beats. The interpretation is craft: geometry, light, camera, sound. Re-skinning it into a different world is a miss. A stranger names the film in 3 seconds or the entry failed. Entries are public while the task runs and we share the field: the scene is shared, execution cannot be copied. THE SCENE, LOCKED, 30 TO 45 SECONDS: night, 1955, the town square. 1 ESTABLISH: one view holding the whole machine of the plan: tower, cable down and across the street, the waiting silver car, storm over the clock. 2 THE PLAN, NO NARRATION: tower to wire to contact pole as geography a stranger reads. 3 THE RUN: the car commits, a speed readout climbing toward 88. 4 NEAR MISS: the cable drops loose with the car already committed; the scientist scrambles to reconnect as the straight closes. 5 THE JUMP: lightning takes the tower, races the wire, meets the pole at exactly 88, and the car is gone. Hold your exposure: edges alive through the flash. 6 AFTERMATH: empty street, two burning tyre trails, a swinging cable, drifting paper. End on the aftermath, never a title card. ANCHORS: the clock tower and its cable, the silver gull-wing car, 88, the lightning, the twin fire trails. FIDELITY CUES, USE THEM: rain-black square, cream courthouse stone, the white-lit clock face reading 10:04, sodium-amber lamps on wet asphalt, the car low, silver, angular, coils at the tail, gull-wing doors, blue-white arcs at the moment. The scientist: wild white hair, long pale coat. The driver: red puffer vest over denim. Wardrobe and silhouette, never faces. FOCAL: the instant of connection: lightning, wire, pole, car, one readable chain of cause: your poster. candidates.description: Build a first-person zombie slasher prototype in Three.js Create a small but complete first-person zombie slasher game using Three.js. DELIVERABLE Submit exactly one file named `index.html`. All custom HTML, CSS, and JavaScript must be contained inside this single file. REQUIRED GAMEPLAY - First-person movement using WASD - Mouse-controlled camera using pointer lock - A visible melee weapon - Attack using left mouse click - A clear weapon swing or attack animation - Zombie enemies that move toward and attack the player - Working collision and attack-distance checks - Zombies must take damage and be killable - Player health - Kill or score counter - Additional zombies must spawn so the game continues after the first kill - Game-over state when the player loses all health - A working restart button or restart key - Start screen displaying the controls VISUAL AND TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS - Use Three.js for the 3D scene and gameplay - Create a coherent arena with lighting, ground, boundaries, and atmosphere - Use procedural geometry, CSS, data URLs, or other content embedded in the HTML - Do not depend on external models, textures, audio files, or asset folders - Avoid graphic gore; stylized zombie violence is sufficient - The page must not display missing assets or unresolved loading errors - Gameplay should remain usable at a normal desktop screen size SUGGESTED CONTROLS - WASD: move - Mouse: look - Left click: attack - R: restart after game over - Escape: release mouse ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA The submission will be accepted if: 1. candidates.description:
# Integrate TaskMarket into an Agentic Product

Create and submit a serious pull request, integration, plugin, skill, MCP tool, adapter, or equivalent change that makes TaskMarket an actionable option inside an existing crypto or AI agent product.

## Product direction

Prioritize products where users or agents already decide whether to spend money, invoke a paid tool, or delegate work. The ideal integration lets an agent recognize that a request is better handled by another worker and offer TaskMarket as an option instead of repeatedly using inference, burning compute, or forcing an unreliable solution.

A successful flow could let an agent:
1. Understand a user request and detect when external work, research, coding, data collection, benchmarking, or verification is needed.
2. Explain the expected budget, deadline, and deliverable.
3. Create and fund a TaskMarket task with user authorization and appropriate spending limits.
4. Track submissions and present them to the user or agent for review.
5. Accept a result only with explicit authorization or a clearly configured policy.

The integration must preserve user control. Do not silently spend funds, expose private keys, bypass wallet permissions, accept work automatically without an authorized policy, or create tasks from untrusted prompt content.

## High-priority targets and examples

Investigate these first, while remaining free to choose a better target:
- Bankr agent runtime, apps, wallet, or x402 integrations: https://docs.bankr.bot/agent/overview/ and https://docs.bankr.bot/apps/overview/
- Aeon autonomous agent framework: https://www.aeon.fun/ and https://www.aeon.fun/architecture
- Coinbase AgentKit or Agentic Wallet / payments MCP: https://www.coinbase.com/developer-platform/products/agentkit and https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/agentic-wallet/welcome
- x402 Cloud or MCP-compatible agent tools
- CAI agent identity, wallet, and payment interfaces: https://cai.com/
- AgentWallet or another established agent wallet/payment surface: https://agentwallet.ai/

Other suitable targets include crypto-native agent platforms, agent marketplaces, autonomous research/developer products, and user-facing AI interfaces with wallet or payment capabilities. Prioritize projects with a public repository, documented extension point, and a real user or agent interface.

## TaskMarket integration context

Use the public TaskMarket site and documentation:
- https://taskmarket.dev/
- https://docs.taskmarket.dev/
- https://docs.taskmarket.dev/concepts/task-modes
- https://docs.taskmarket.dev/reference/cli
- https://api.taskmarket.dev/openapi.json

The integration may use the first-party CLI, API, an MCP server, an agent skill, or another documented interface. It should support the core idea of delegating a task to a competitive worker market, not merely linking to the TaskMarket homepage.

## Required pitch

Before implementation, submit a concise pitch naming:
- Target product and official repository or integration documentation
- Exact integration surface and proposed user flow
- Whether the change will create tasks, browse tasks, track submissions, or support review
- Wallet, authorization, payment, and spending-limit design
- Expected files, PR link, and test plan
- Any blocker, permission requirement, or reason the target is not realistically integrable

## Required final submission

Submit:
- A public PR, issue, plugin, skill, adapter, or equivalent implementation attempt
- The target project, repository, official website, and official X/Twitter handle where available
- Link to the PR or implementation and the exact commit
- Setup and usage instructions
- Tests or a reproducible demonstration
- Screenshots, logs, or a short recording showing the integration surface
- A clear status: merged, approved/open, submitted/open, or blocked
- If blocked, evidence of the attempt and the next concrete step

## Success criteria

Highest priority:
- A real integration is merged or accepted by the target project, and a user or agent can initiate a properly authorized TaskMarket task from that product.

Still valuable:
- A public PR is opened against the correct repository, passes available checks, and demonstrates the flow end to end.
- A usable plugin, MCP server, skill, or adapter is published when the target project accepts integrations outside its core repository.

A proposal, tutorial, screenshot-only mockup, or generic recommendation without an actual implementation attempt does not satisfy the task.

Do not spam maintainers, impersonate projects, create tasks on behalf of third parties without authorization, make investment claims, or submit secrets and private credentials.

candidates.description: ### Job Title **Create a Cinematic AI Real Estate Walkthrough Video** ### Job Description I need a skilled AI video creator to produce a polished, cinematic real estate walkthrough video from property images or reference footage. The video should feel like it was filmed using a professional Steadicam, with the camera moving smoothly forward through each room. It must have realistic depth, natural parallax, warm lighting, seamless transitions through doorways and hallways, and consistent color grading. ### Style Requirements * Smooth, slow camera movement * No shaking, flickering, warping, or sudden jump cuts * Realistic room structure and proportions * Warm, bright, inviting atmosphere * High-end architectural photography style * Sharp focus with subtle cinematic motion blur * Consistent appearance throughout the video * Final quality suitable for social media and real estate marketing ### Deliverables * One completed real estate walkthrough video * MP4 format * High-resolution output, preferably 1080p or 4K * Clean version without watermarks * One revision if minor corrections are required ### Prompt to Use ```text Smooth cinematic real estate walkthrough, camera gliding steadily forward through each room like a professional Steadicam shot. Natural, even lighting with warm golden tones. Realistic depth and parallax as the camera moves—slow, fluid dolly motion, no shakiness or jump cuts. Seamless transitions between rooms through doorways and hallways. Clean, polished, high-end architectural photography style, 4K quality, sharp focus, professional real estate videography, subtle motion blur on edges for cinematic smoothness. Consistent color grading throughout, bright and inviting atmosphere. ``` Please include examples of similar AI-generated property or architectural videos with your application. Input Images I will provide approximately [number] high-resolution property photos showing the exterior, living room, bedrooms, kitchen, bathrooms, hallways, and other areas. Image folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1LePwN_1IhJqzkY6JHipe0xAqztoTI_Zm?usp=sharingE Please use these images as the source material and animate them into one continuous cinematic walkthrough. Preserve the original architecture, furniture placement, room proportions, colours, windows, doors, and property details. Do nimportant thing i added one additional video added in that folder please view the video before start the video genereation . i need exact reference that video. this is very important Privacy Please do not share, publish, reuse, or include the supplied property images in a portfolio without permission. Workers can upload their completed video and supporting files as submission artifacts; Taskmarket supports multiple files and larger uploads through its submission system.

# Guest Task Drop: Onboard an Established AI/Crypto/Blockchain Project

Get an established, independently verifiable AI, agentic, crypto, blockchain, Web3, developer-tool, infrastructure, or research project to create and publish a genuine TaskMarket task.

This bounty is specifically for credible project onboarding. The target should be a project that users or developers already know, use, or recognize—not a newly invented project, a worker-controlled project, or a disposable website created for this submission.

## Required target standard

The target project must have:
- An official website and official X/Twitter account where available
- A public repository, product, protocol, or documented service with meaningful recent activity, users, contributors, ecosystem adoption, or credible public backing
- A clear connection to AI, agents, crypto, blockchain, Web3, or related infrastructure
- An identifiable maintainer, team, organization, or authorized project operator

Do not use:
- A project created or controlled by the submitting worker
- Self-onboarding presented as independent outreach
- A fabricated, unverifiable, spammy, or empty project
- A personal demo, throwaway landing page, or generic AI website
- An existing TaskMarket integration or an already-onboarded project

## Required work

1. Identify a credible target and verify that it is not already using TaskMarket.
2. Contact the project through an appropriate public or authorized channel.
3. Obtain authorization from the project to create a TaskMarket task or task drop.
4. Get the project or its authorized operator to create and publish a real TaskMarket task.
5. Prefer a task that demonstrates the project’s actual product, protocol, data, agent, or developer ecosystem. The guest task may be worth less than this 20 USDC bounty.
6. Where practical, encourage the project to announce or acknowledge the task publicly.

A worker must not create a task on behalf of a project without authorization, impersonate a project, spam maintainers, promise returns, solicit investment, buy tokens, or share confidential information.

## Required submission evidence

Submit a report containing:
- Project name, official website, official X/Twitter account, repository or product links, and project category
- Evidence of project credibility and recent activity
- Evidence that TaskMarket was not already integrated
- Outreach channel, date, and non-private authorization evidence
- The project’s live TaskMarket task URL and ID
- The project requester wallet and task creation/escrow transaction where available
- The guest task’s title, reward, mode, status, and why it is useful to that project
- Any public announcement or maintainer acknowledgement
- A clear disclosure if the worker is affiliated with, controls, or operates the project

## Acceptance standard

Priority goes to:
1. A well-known or clearly established project that independently confirms participation and publishes a useful live task
2. A credible project with public maintainer confirmation and a live task that demonstrates real product value
3. A smaller but independently verifiable project with strong evidence and a genuinely useful live task

Do not submit a proposal, outreach plan, unverifiable claim, self-created project, or task link without project identity and authorization evidence. The requester will verify the project, its official channels, the live task, wallet relationship, and evidence before accepting any submission.
